summary.headline: eMudhra Q1 FY27 total income rose 28% YoY to INR 1,925 million, with EBITDA up 40% to INR 504 million at a 26.2% margin.
summary.overview: Total income grew 27.8% YoY to INR 1,925 million, of which about 13 points came from the Cryptas acquisition (about INR 200 million revenue). Enterprise Solutions grew about 50% YoY and made up 65% of income, while Trust Services declined temporarily as legacy token demand fell ahead of a September security-standard transition. PAT rose 28% to INR 320 million (16.6% margin), and management kept its FY27 guidance of 18% organic growth and 25% PAT growth unchanged.

segments.name: Enterprise Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,623 million, about 50% YoY growth and 65% of total income; organic product growth about 25% after Cryptas contribution, per management. Management cited higher margin mix from lower token sales.

segments.name: Trust Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 284 million with a temporary decline as partners destocked legacy tokens before a September transition. Management estimated INR 5-7 crore of token volume was lost; token gross margin is about 10%.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Growth of about 5% YoY, supported by new US customers; margins are roughly 18-20%, similar to historical levels.

segments.name: Cryptas (Europe)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR 20 crore in a seasonally weak quarter; first CertiNext sale to a German data center operator and first mSigner/PrimeSign deployment for an Austrian municipality. Management expects Cryptas to turn profitable in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: 18% organic growth in total income and 25% PAT growth.
Management expects EBITDA margin around 25% and PAT margin around 16-16.5% going forward, as added sales hires weigh on costs.
Trust Service revenue likely stays lower in Q2 FY27 as legacy token demand remains weak; bottom-line impact described as limited given low token margins.
Three-year target (FY27-FY29) of doubling PAT, with about 18-20% organic revenue growth per year; Enterprise Solutions expected at 20-25% growth per year and Trust Services 15-20%.
UAE Trust Service (QTSP) licence expected around end of Q1 or start of Q2 FY27, after which launch is planned.
Expects the Cryptas loss to end in FY27 and the European subsidiary (BV) to be profitable this year; ROE expected to be maintained at about 14.5-15%.
capex_capacity: Token supply constrained: ePass token recertification by CCA submitted and largely complete, pending CCA action; management expects ePass certification by about September, after which volumes should recover.
New Innate token is certified but volumes are low because capacity is limited.

Cryptas integration of eMudhra's own CA and CLM IP replacing third-party products (such as Keyfactor) developed over the last six to seven months; this is intended to reduce cost and shift transfer pricing to India.
Added senior sales hires across geographies (USD 200,000-300,000 per person), which will weigh on near-term margins.
demand_pricing: Trust Services: partners destocked legacy tokens ahead of the September global transition to FIPS 140-3, which reduced volumes.

SecurePass in India: large bank or government deals typically start at INR 4-6 crore and can exceed INR 10 crore per bank for full PIM/PAM suites; compliance mandates from RBI-type regulators and SEBI-type regulators are cited as drivers.
US products: university federation (Common) onboarding is live, with about 1,000-1,500 certificates issued daily; IoT/PKI and SSL-expiry (47-day) demand are cited as pipeline drivers.
Agentic AI identity and signing is described as an early-stage opportunity; management said quantification is not possible yet and pilots are expected within about a year.
PrivaTrust consent-management modules are being piloted; a broader data discovery and classification suite is planned, with focus on India under the DPDP Act.

financial_highlights.change: About 13 points of 28% total income growth
